chapter: Trent's band: Arkansas, Dallas and the Adolphus
title: Inventing the slide sax and a machine-gun-shaped instrument
summary: Trained in manual arts, he builds a saxophone-mouthpiece instrument shaped like a machine gun during the Dallas job and patents it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah, of course that's the master back there on the drums. A.G. and you can see how I had the slide saxophone there.

Well you know I had four years of manual training and woodwork and metal work in high school in Gibbs. I always wanted to play differently and be different from the other guys. They used to say if you played a brass instrument you couldn't play a reed, they used to say that. Of course, guys like Benny Carter did. But way back they used to say that you couldn't do two instruments. But what I really wanted when I made this thing up, it was an awful looking thing, badly sorted and of course it took me a long time to get it so I could play a real tune on it.
THAT ANYBODY ELSE HAD EVER PLAYED BEFORE
Well, I had this idea, but I didn't do anything about until after I had been at the Adolphis.

That was the thing that was going around in those days that you couldn't play a saxophone mouthpiece, a brass or vice versa. And I wanted to prove that you could do that and I guess I did and I just, now the thing that made me want to have this instrument like it is, if you notice, it looks something like a machine gun. I wanted to have a machine gun and an instrument. I wanted this instrument for two reasons. We went into wild and wooley Texas and I wanted something for protection. And I learned I wouldn't be able to get a patent on it.
If I had as a machine gun. So this was developed after we got into the Adolphis.
PATENTED, YEAH. WHAT KIND OF THINGS DID YOU PLAY.
I was playing ballads and I played, later, I started playing with both a trombone mouthpiece and a (inaudible) on "The Man With A Funny Horn" was done with a trombone mouthpiece.
YOU WEREN'T DOING THIS WITH TRENT? THIS WAS LATER ON.
YOU WERE STRICKLY, THIS WAS STRICKLY WITH A SAXOPHONE MOUTHPIECE. WERE YOU PLAYING WHOLE ARRANGEMENTS WITH THE BAND OR DID YOU KEEP ON DOING REGULAR PIECES.
I would do little solos and then Jeeter and I would do, I used to put his clarinet in this end of my mouth and my trombone hand he would finger it and then that would be that.
